subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw scope this issue to boundary-based steering plus the remaining ordinary-message admission fix, or pursue a full pause/abort/resume soft-steer lifecycle beyond current Codex `turn/steer` semantics?
rationale: Current main and Codex support same-turn steering at explicit active-turn boundaries, but true mid-generation interruption and resume would change runtime lifecycle, fallback, and session-state contracts across channels.

options.title: Refresh Boundary-Based Admission
options.body: Rebase or replace PR 89238, preserve PR 98126 behavior, and keep true pause/resume as a later explicit design.

options.title: Document Explicit Controls Only
options.body: Keep `/steer` and command-lane steering as the supported active path and document that ordinary messages queue until a broader design is sponsored.

options.title: Sponsor Full Soft-Steer Design
options.body: Design a new lifecycle for aborting or pausing active generation, preserving partial output, injecting input, and resuming across Codex and non-Codex runtimes.

recommendation.title: Refresh Boundary-Based Admission
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace PR 89238, preserve PR 98126 behavior, and keep true pause/resume as a later explicit design.

likelyOwner.reason: They are connected to the recent steering/admission history and adjacent session-state work that the decision must preserve.
